title: The psychology of colour
text: Companies spend millions choosing the right colours {{1}} their brands, believing that colour affects how we feel {{2}} what we buy. Red, for example, is said to stimulate appetite, {{3}} is why so many fast-food chains use it. Blue, on the other {{4}} , is associated with trust and calm, which explains {{5}} popularity with banks. However, cultural differences matter: white symbolises purity in some cultures {{6}} death in others. Psychologists warn that the effects of colour are modest, {{7}} , and that context matters more {{8}} colour itself. A bright red bank would still seem strange, though.
